cites.quote: Likud leaders proposed yesterday that Menahem Begin be [invited] by President Ephraim Katzir to form a government

After hearing from Bar-Lev of Alignment support for the tradition that the head of the largest party be [invited] first to form a government, Prof. Katzir asked if that meant the Alignment was not proposing its own candidate. Bar-Lev responded, "At this stage, we are not."
Leaders of the Democratic Movement for Change and of the National Religious [Party] ... asked President Ephraim [Katzir] yesterday to select Menahem Begin to head the next government.
Leaders of the Democratic Movement for Change and of the National Religious [Party] ... asked President Ephraim [Katzir] yesterday to select Menahem Begin to head the next government.

entries.noteEn: Named no candidate in the report; stated the President was not bound to ask the largest party first.

cites.quote: Rakah, however, said the President was not legally required to first ask the head of the largest party in the new Knesset.
Agudat Yisrael and [Shlomzion] proposed Likud leader Menahem [Begin].

Agudat Yisrael and [Shlomzion] proposed Likud leader Menahem [Begin]. ... Ariel [Sharon], head of [Shlomzion], appeared despite his announcement that he is joining the Likud, since the merger is not yet [official].

entries.noteEn: Asked for "a moderate statesman" and gave two Alignment MKs as examples.

cites.quote: A [Sheli] spokesman said its delegation had asked the President to select a "moderate statesman, such as Haim Zadok (present Justice minister) or Yitzhak Navon (another Alignment MK)," to form a government.

entries.noteEn: Reported as support for a Begin-led government.

cites.quote: In his talk with the President yesterday, Flatto Sharon voiced his support for a government led by Menahem Begin
The Alignment will appear today, followed by the NRP and the DMC tomorrow and smaller parties through Sunday.
President Ephraim Katzir yesterday received MK-elect Samuel Flatto Sharon, thus concluding his consultations with representatives of all parties successful in the elections.
הואיל נשיא המדינה, מכוח סמכותו ועל־פי המלצתן של סיעות בכנסת המייצגות רוב מכריע של חבריה, להטיל עלי את התפקיד להרכיב את הממשלה

notes: Totals are sums of the per-list entries above, not a figure published by the President. No official tally was retrieved.

Four one-seat lists (Poalei Agudat Yisrael, Independent Liberals, Civil Rights Movement, United Arab List) were consulted on 3 or 5 June per the schedule, but their positions were not found in the issues read (gap).
Primary record to retrieve: Israel State Archives presidential file נ-571/13, "הנשיאים קציר ונבון – תיקי הרכבת ממשלות – הרכבת הממשלה ה-18" (cited in isa-navon-1981).

events.textEn: President Katzir consulted the lists elected to the Ninth Knesset.
events.textHe: הנשיא קציר התייעץ עם הרשימות שנבחרו לכנסת התשיעית.

cites.quote: were the first to be received by the President for party consultations
thus concluding his consultations with representatives of all parties successful in the elections

events.textEn: Katzir tasked Menachem Begin with forming a government (21 days).
events.textHe: קציר הטיל על מנחם בגין להרכיב ממשלה (21 ימים).

cites.quote: ביום כ"א בסיון תשל"ז, 7 ביוני 1977, הואיל כבוד נשיא המדינה להטיל עלי את התפקיד להרכיב ממשלה.
"I have consulted with all the parties that will be represented in the Ninth Knesset, and I decided to ask Mr. Begin to form a government," said the President
Israeli law gives Begin 21 days to form a government and an additional 21 days if needed.

events.textEn: Begin presented the 18th government; the Knesset approved it, 63–53, and the ministers made their declarations.
events.textHe: בגין הציג את הממשלה ה־18; הכנסת הביעה בה אמון ברוב של 63 מול 53, והשרים הצהירו אמונים.

cites.quote: בעד ההצעה להביע אמון בממשלה – 63 / נגד – 53 / ההצעה להביע אמון בממשלה נתקבלה.
his 63-53 margin was strictly along party lines. Voting for the government were Likud, the National Religious Party (NRP) and Aguda bloc, Moshe Dayan and Samuel Flatto-Sharon.

events.textEn: Egyptian President Anwar Sadat visited Jerusalem and addressed the Knesset.
events.textHe: נשיא מצרים אנואר סאדאת ביקר בירושלים ונאם בכנסת.

cites.quote: The main event during the term of the ninth Knesset was the visit of Egyptian President Anwar Sadat to Jerusalem in November 1977, and his appearance in the Knesset.
He served as Speaker of the Knesset during Egyptian President Anwar Sadat's visit to Israel.
visit of Egyptian President Anwar Sadat to Jerusalem (November 1977)

events.textEn: The Peace Now movement was founded.

cites.quote: "Peace Now" was founded in 1978.
Peace Now movement is founded

events.textEn: Israel launched Operation Litani in southern Lebanon after the Coastal Road terror attack.
events.textHe: ישראל פתחה במבצע ליטני בדרום לבנון בעקבות פיגוע כביש החוף.

cites.quote: following which Israel launched the Litani Operation in Lebanon.
the Litani Operation took place in March 1978
Operation Litani
The Israeli withdrawal was completed in June 1978

notes: Withdrawal date is not labelled a ceasefire date. No trigger added without agreement of the original two selection chronologies.
The Defense Ministry chronology explicitly links Operation Litani to the Coastal Road massacre; ECF dates completion of withdrawal to June 1978, distinct from a ceasefire.
ציר הזמן של משרד הביטחון קושר את מבצע ליטני לפיגוע כביש החוף; ECF מתארך את השלמת הנסיגה ליוני 1978, ואינו מציג זאת כמועד הפסקת אש.

events.textEn: Terrorists hijacked a bus and murdered passengers in the Coastal Road massacre.
events.textHe: מחבלים חטפו אוטובוס ורצחו נוסעים בפיגוע כביש החוף.

cites.quote: a group of eleven PLO-Fatah terrorists
in March 1978 there was an attack along the Coastal Road
A bus is hijacked by terrorists on the coastal road
March 11, 1978

events.textEn: The Knesset approved the Camp David Accords.
events.textHe: הכנסת אישרה את הסכמי קמפ דייוויד.

cites.quote: The Knesset [approved] the Camp David Accords in September 1978, by a large majority
he abstained from the vote on the Camp David Accords
ב- 27 בספטמבר 1978 אישרה הכנסת את הסכמי קמפ דייוויד ברוב של 84 מול 19 מתנגדים, ו-17 נמנעים.
Camp David Accords (September 1978)
בעד – 84; נגד – 19; נמנעו – 17. הצעת הסיכום נתקבלה.

notes: The official plenum record confirms 84–19–17. Month precision retained: the sitting dated 27 September ran overnight and ended at 03:32.
MFA independently selects the accords/treaty as a national event; the Knesset history supplies the parliamentary approval act. MFA is not evidence for the approval vote or its tally.

events.textEn: The Knesset approved the peace treaty with Egypt, the first between Israel and an Arab state.

cites.quote: After less than a year and a half, the first peace agreement between Israel and an Arab state was signed. The Knesset [approved] ... the peace treaty with Egypt in March 1979.
and also abstained from the vote to ratify the peace treaty, which was held in March 1979.
On 26 March 1979, Israel and Egypt signed a peace treaty

הפצצת הכור העיראקי ב-7 ביוני על ידי חיל האוויר הישראלי
Three weeks before the election, Begin approved an Israeli air strike on the Iraqi nuclear installation, which was soon to have become active.
Israel Air Force destroys Iraqi nuclear reactor
